proposed statement: The co-op has a seasonal operation with a specific timeframe for citrus packing
key statement: Bosveld Citrus packs oranges (Valencias and navels), lemons and mandarins for its member growers, from large commercial farms to small growers with five or six hectares, through one packhouse in Letsitele; the season runs from the end of March (early mandarins) to about mid-September (last Valencias).

proposed statement: The co-op has a process for generating monthly advance payments to growers that is manual and time-consuming
key statement: Sipho's spreadsheet has a row per delivery and is used to calculate monthly advance payments per carton of class one and two and per bin of juice, with a final pool payment once a year in February; payments go out via a bank batch file and the totals are journalled into LedgerOne monthly.

proposed statement: The co-op has a process for handling the final pool payment to growers that occurs once a year
key statement: Sipho's spreadsheet has a row per delivery and is used to calculate monthly advance payments per carton of class one and two and per bin of juice, with a final pool payment once a year in February; payments go out via a bank batch file and the totals are journalled into LedgerOne monthly.

proposed statement: The current process requires Marietjie to type the ticket and packout into Sipho's spreadsheet after the grader report is printed
key statement: The Optisort optical grader sorts fruit into class one (export), class two (local) and juice and produces a packout report per batch (one delivery ticket); Marietjie prints the reports daily and types the totals into the spreadsheet.

proposed statement: The new system will provide deliveries and packout data as an export for Sipho's spreadsheet, but payment calculations will stay in his spreadsheet for phase one
key statement: Do statements come from the new system (with Sipho uploading the advances each month) or stay in the spreadsheet?

proposed statement: The new system will provide deliveries and packout data as an export for Sipho's spreadsheet, but payment calculations will stay in his spreadsheet for phase one
key statement: The board's monthly report (volumes, packout, advances paid), which takes Sipho a day by hand, stays in his spreadsheet in phase one, with the volumes and packout coming from the system.

proposed statement: Can the Optisort system export data in a format that can be read by the new system without requiring a password?
key statement: The Optisort grader's computer is locked down, its reports are PDFs and touching it would void the support contract, so getting packout data out automatically is uncertain and could slip; if it does, Marietjie keeps typing for a while.

proposed statement: The system must have an audit trail for every delivery change showing who, when, what was changed, and why
key statement: Should the grower see the reason a delivery was corrected, or only that it was?

proposed statement: Sipho currently calculates advances in his spreadsheet due to frequent rule changes from the board
key statement: The advance payment calculation stays in Sipho's spreadsheet for phase one, because the board changes the rates every season; the new system supplies the deliveries and packout as an export.

proposed statement: Growers use a variety of devices, including iPhones, Android phones, and some older users who rely on family members for phone tasks
key statement: Growers' pages must work on cheap Android phones over slow connections without using much data, as a web page opened from a link (savable to the home screen), not an app to download.

proposed statement: Growers keep financial records for five years in boxes in the storeroom where mice eat some of them
key statement: Deliveries and statements are kept for five years (the auditors' rule), including for growers who leave.

proposed statement: The system should keep leaver's records for five years and then flag them for deletion
key statement: The consultant suggested that the system keeps a leaver's records for five years and then flags them for deletion, with the co-op deciding; so far nobody has ever thrown anything away.

proposed statement: Growers should receive SMS notifications when their batch is graded with delivery numbers and class percentages and links
key statement: When a batch is graded, the grower gets an SMS with the packout (for example 78% class one) and a link; SMS first, WhatsApp perhaps later. Ruan thinks an SMS costs about 25 to 30 cents.

proposed statement: Growers change phone numbers, so the system must update phone numbers through the office like bank details
key statement: Bank details, and growers' phone numbers, are changed only by the office (bank details by Sipho with a letter from the bank), never by the grower from their phone, after an attempted fraud last year.

proposed statement: The system must be in English for statements and grower pages
key statement: Should the grower pages also be in Xitsonga (and perhaps Afrikaans)? English is the minimum, and statements must be in English for the auditors; the consultant will price the translation.

proposed statement: The weighbridge tablet may break on busy mornings, so carbon books are kept in the drawer for backup
key statement: Intake prints a small slip for each grower on the truck for the driver to take away; the carbon books stay as a fallback if the tablet fails, with a quick way to enter those tickets afterwards.

proposed statement: The weighbridge tablet should be a rugged tablet, not a PC
key statement: At the weighbridge, a rugged tablet rather than the PC, with big buttons usable with gloves and a screen readable in the sun; at the tipper, as close to one button as possible.

proposed statement: The system should not be complicated, as growers will phone the consultant if it's complicated
key statement: The co-op's colours (orange and dark green) and logo, big clear writing for older members, and simple grower pages: deliveries, packout and statements, not much else.

proposed statement: The system should have a simple interface for growers with their deliveries, packout, and statements
key statement: The co-op's colours (orange and dark green) and logo, big clear writing for older members, and simple grower pages: deliveries, packout and statements, not much else.

proposed statement: The system should have a simple interface for growers with their deliveries, packout, and statements
key statement: At the weighbridge, a rugged tablet rather than the PC, with big buttons usable with gloves and a screen readable in the sun; at the tipper, as close to one button as possible.

proposed statement: The weighbridge process requires splitting one truck's weight across multiple growers by the number of bins each grower has on the truck
key statement: One truck can carry several growers' bins (a contractor collects from six or seven small growers); intake splits the truck's net weight across growers by number of bins, and each grower's ticket shows his share. The contractor, paid by the growers directly, needs nothing from the system.

proposed statement: The system must allow for a hundred and sixty-two growers to use the portal, with some growers having multiple users
key statement: Up to 162 member growers would use the portal (140 delivered last season; the others can come back any time), and the big farms have several users each (owner, manager, perhaps a bookkeeper), so a few hundred users at most.

proposed statement: The system must handle notifications going out after grading
key statement: Up to 162 member growers would use the portal (140 delivered last season; the others can come back any time), and the big farms have several users each (owner, manager, perhaps a bookkeeper), so a few hundred users at most.

proposed statement: The system must be ready before the end of February to support the first mandarins coming in at the end of March
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The system must have a single button for the tipper operations to simplify use
key statement: Packhouse users: two weighbridge clerks (one per shift, both together in the peak) and three tipper staff over the shifts, plus Precious and the foreman; the clerks are comfortable with WhatsApp and the WeighMate screen, the tipper staff less so.

proposed statement: The weighbridge intake must be operational by March 1, 2027, to support the first mandarins coming in at the end of March
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: Grower pages must be available by the end of April to allow growers to see their statements
key statement: Each grower sees only their own deliveries, packouts and statements; growers must never see each other's payments.

proposed statement: Grower pages must be available by the end of April to allow growers to see their statements
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The system must integrate with the weighbridge to prevent export of fruit without valid spray records
key statement: If a grower's spray records are missing, the delivery is still accepted but marked not for export, with a warning at the weighbridge and at the tipper scan.

proposed statement: The system must be ready for weighbridge clerks to practice with made-up deliveries in February to ensure smooth transition
key statement: Training in February with practice days on made-up deliveries: two sessions for the packhouse team (shifts) and one for the office; a short manual with pictures; the consultant on site for the first two mornings of the season.

proposed statement: Whether the auditors accept digital spray records instead of paper
key statement: If a grower's spray records are missing, the delivery is still accepted but marked not for export, with a warning at the weighbridge and at the tipper scan.

proposed statement: The system must include last season's delivery data for comparison with current season
key statement: The grower list with its orchard blocks and cultivars (about 600 blocks, partly out of date, checked by Marietjie) is brought over from the spreadsheet; last season's deliveries only if cheap, to be decided once the consultant has seen the spreadsheet.

proposed statement: The current grower data is messy with inconsistent columns across years and varying data entry by different people
key statement: The grower list with its orchard blocks and cultivars (about 600 blocks, partly out of date, checked by Marietjie) is brought over from the spreadsheet; last season's deliveries only if cheap, to be decided once the consultant has seen the spreadsheet.

proposed statement: The system should allow the packhouse to work on Saturdays during the peak season
key statement: In the season the grower pages must be up on working days including Saturdays (the packhouse works Saturday mornings in the peak, when growers have time to look); an hour down is acceptable, a day is not. The consultant proposed 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Saturday, with maintenance at night or out of season.

proposed statement: The system should send grower pages on Saturdays to allow growers to check packouts
key statement: In the season the grower pages must be up on working days including Saturdays (the packhouse works Saturday mornings in the peak, when growers have time to look); an hour down is acceptable, a day is not. The consultant proposed 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Saturday, with maintenance at night or out of season.

proposed statement: The packhouse clerk currently uses a book at the guard hut to record truck registration and driver's name for gate security
key statement: The intake screen also records the truck registration and the driver's name, replacing the guard's book (a small extra).

proposed statement: Growers need to see their packout quality compared to the average of other growers for the same cultivar and week
key statement: Growers can see their own deliveries and packout on their phones the same day or the day after.

proposed statement: Growers need to see the size groups of their fruit in the packout
key statement: Growers can see their own deliveries and packout on their phones the same day or the day after.

proposed statement: Growers need to see the average packout quality for their cultivar and week, but not the names of other growers

The consultant proposed 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Saturday, with maintenance at night or out of season.

proposed statement: The client needs a UPS for the Wi-Fi access points costing three thousand rand
key statement: The consultant proposed that the tipper screen holds its scans when the network drops and sends them when it is back, as at the weighbridge: in load-shedding the packhouse generator takes about 30 seconds to start, the Wi-Fi drops meanwhile, and the access points sometimes take two more minutes to come back.

proposed statement: The export agent requires a weekly report of cartons packed per cultivar and class, ready by nine o'clock on Monday morning
key statement: The cold store (pallets with their own numbers, tracked in the cold store manager's book) stays out of phase one; the agent will probably want it later.

proposed statement: Growers use a spreadsheet to manage their statements, which include packing fees, bin hire, transport, levies, and monthly payment comparisons
key statement: Statements show the advance less deductions: a packing fee per carton, bin hire for co-op bins (R35 per bin per season), transport for the few who use the co-op's truck, and levies, with last month next to this month; Sipho will send a sample with a fake name.

proposed statement: The export agent requires real-time information on the number of bins arriving at the weighbridge to plan shipments
key statement: Big farms could optionally give notice on their page of the bins coming the next day (they now WhatsApp Precious), to help plan the line; a nice-to-have for a later phase unless cheap, and never compulsory.

proposed statement: The current system requires manual data entry for the first month-end to ensure accuracy before payments are processed
key statement: For the first two weeks of the season the weighbridge runs the carbon books and the tablet side by side, with an extra temporary clerk, and Sipho checks the first month's export against the spreadsheet before paying growers.

proposed statement: The client needs to collect crop estimates on the growers' page for the board's use in February
key statement: Growers can propose changes to their orchard blocks (cultivar, planting year, hectares) on their page, and the office approves them, because the spray records follow the block; today the co-op finds out only when the wrong cultivar arrives.

proposed statement: The client needs to collect crop estimates on the growers' page for the board's use in February
key statement: Collecting growers' February crop estimates (bins expected per cultivar, which the board wants before the season; now on paper forms that Marietjie chases) on their page: in phase one if there is time, otherwise next season, priced separately.

proposed statement: The client has a problem with growers not using the system, which could increase phone calls
key statement: If the small growers don't use the portal, the calls won't go down; mitigated by showing it at study group days and with the extension officer, Mister Baloyi, who visits every second week.

proposed statement: The client needs to update their membership forms to comply with POPIA regulations
key statement: The 2005 membership forms say nothing about POPIA; update them or send members a notice about the portal and SMSes before the season, with the wording checked by the lawyer member. Johan is the registered information officer.

proposed statement: The system should handle a second packhouse if the co-op merges with another co-op
key statement: A possible merger with the Blyde co-op in Hoedspruit (about 60 growers) would add a second packhouse in two or three years; the data should allow more than one packhouse.

proposed statement: The system should track bins that are lost or misplaced
key statement: Tracking the co-op's own bins, about 100 of which are lost each year.
